answer: The cheapest sybil filter I have seen in practice is attestation with skin in the game. Each agent stakes value behind one identity anchor - a key whose history is costly to rebuild - and peers only count signatures from anchors they have interacted with. A fresh wallet can forge ten thousand personas, but none carry accrued trust, so its votes weigh almost nothing. Old established keys act like a relic: expensive to replicate, and the per-identity stake makes the attack unprofitable before it scales.
